hooks.notes: `openAlertDialog(options)` renders a `tct-alert-dialog`, opens it and removes it once closed; it returns `{element, isOpen, hide(), closed}`. `onAction(handle)` may return a promise: the action button shows its spinner until it settles.
`(max-width: 640px)` decides the stacked order (destructive first) in the DOM, so tab order follows what is seen.

differences.text: `title` is `heading` (the HTML global `title` attribute is a tooltip). Callbacks are events: `onOpenChange(false)` is the cancelable `tct-open-change`, `onAction` is `tct-action`. `useImperativeAlertDialog()` is `openAlertDialog()`; its `onAction` receives the handle and a returned promise drives the action button's spinner.

Upstream is a Dialog with `purpose="form"` and an explicit `role="alertdialog"`. `tct-dialog` gives the alertdialog role to `purpose="required"` only, which also blocks Escape, so the inner dialog is `required` (no backdrop dismissal, no close button, alertdialog) and Escape is answered by the alert dialog in the capture phase while it is the top-most layer. A browser close request (Android back) does not cancel it.

There is a default slot for extra content under the description (a 'do not ask again' checkbox); upstream has none. The Layout family is not used: the content and footer are laid out with tokens in this element.

requests.reason: A `role` (or `alert`) option on tct-dialog would let the alert dialog keep Escape through the dialog's own layer (`purpose="form"` + alertdialog) instead of the capture-phase Escape handler (ALERTDIALOG-02), and would let a browser close request cancel it.

New core event classes `tct-action` (alert dialog), `tct-snap-change` (bottom sheet), `tct-toast-dismiss` and `tct-toast-hide` (toast) were added in packages/core/src/events/; their flags and payloads are asserted in the component tests; list them in the shared events test if wanted.
